Consider the following code segment, which is intended to create a `String` that consists of the last character in `word` and assign it to the variable `lastChar`.

```java
String word = /* initialization not shown */; // line 1
int len = word.length(); // line 2
String lastChar = word.substring(len); // line 3
```

Which of the following best describes why this code segment will not work as intended?

answers.text: `substring` needs to be called with two parameters, so the method call in line 3 should be changed to `word.substring(len, len + 1)`.
answers.explanation: The one-parameter form of `substring` is valid. Also, starting at `len` gives the empty string; using `(len, len + 1)` would use an end index beyond the string length.

answers.text: `len` is not the correct index of the last character in `word`, so the method call in line 3 should be changed to `word.substring(len - 1)`.
answers.explanation: Correct. String indices run from `0` to `length() - 1`. To get the last character using the one-parameter version of `substring`, the starting index should be `len - 1`, not `len`.

answers.text: `len` is not the correct index of the last character in `word`, so the method call in line 3 should be changed to `word.substring(len + 1)`.
answers.explanation: `len + 1` is even farther beyond the last valid character index and cannot identify the last character.

answers.text: `substring` cannot be called with a variable as the parameter, so the method call in line 3 should be changed to `word.substring(word.length())`.
answers.explanation: A variable is a valid argument to `substring`; `word.length()` equals `len`, so this still starts at the position after the last character and produces the empty string.

questions.explanation: String indices run from `0` to `length() - 1`. To get the last character using the one-parameter version of `substring`, the starting index should be `len - 1`, not `len`.

answers.text: `"a"` is the first character in `word`.
answers.explanation: If `"a"` is first, `aLoc` is `0`; `substring(0, 0)` is empty and `substring(1)` is valid, so the first character is removed correctly.

answers.text: `"a"` is the last character in `word`.
answers.explanation: If `"a"` is last, `substring(aLoc + 1)` is `substring(word.length())`, which is valid and returns the empty string.

answers.text: `word` does not contain the character `"a"`.
answers.explanation: Correct. If `word` does not contain `"a"`, then `indexOf("a")` returns `-1`. The call `word.substring(0, -1)` uses an invalid index and causes a runtime error.

answers.text: `word` contains only a sequence of multiple `"a"` characters.
answers.explanation: A word containing several `"a"` characters still has a valid first occurrence index; the code removes that first occurrence without an index error.
